statement: For every infinite ν and |H|≤ν there is a fixed E_H of size≤ν containing H such that every set-sized transfinite tower of finite nonsingular relative presentations from H maps to E_H preserving H. Every nonidentity element of such a tower survives in a quotient of size≤ν. Thus any actual two-dimensional classifying complex admitting a finite homology-equivalence block filtration over a ≤ν-cell core has residually ≤ν fundamental group.
manuscript_pages_settled: A3(iii): all transfinite finite nonsingular attachment-block strategies retain small images; positive residual frontier requires an infinite simultaneous block
notes: The fixed target preserves the initial coefficient group; elementwise residual targets E_K may vary. The residual proof closes a chosen word under countably many coefficient dependencies, then reorders these blocks first and uses coefficient injection. No arbitrary relative exponent isomorphism is asserted to admit a finite-block filtration. The target need not be torsion-free or two-dimensional. No existing result IDs were changed.
